NID HARYANA
eNav
Time, motion and direction—a smart wearable
system built around the idea that a rider’s attention is
more scarce than screen space.
Time, motion and direction
The project framed navigation as a focused wearable
experience. Instead of reproducing a phone screen,
eNav shows only the information needed in motion.
Digital prototyping
ESP-32 DevKit V1 became the working board after
exploring both ESP and Raspberry Pi systems. The
display and wiring were assembled into an early
functional prototype.
Test run through Arduino IDE
Code was run through Arduino IDE to understand how
each instruction affected the board and display. Mock
outputs were checked through the serial monitor.
Making a custom PCB
After studying how PCB layers route overlapping and
direct connections, a custom circuit was laid out and
hand-built on a DIY soldering board.
Plug-and-play final PCB
The custom board compressed the loose wiring into a
compact plug-and-play connection for the ESP-32 and
display.
Google Navigation interface
A complete Google Navigation view would require the
Navigation API embedded in the app. Mock code
validated the information path before that integration.
Phone-to-display data
A third-party phone application supplied live
navigation data to the ESP-32, establishing the
connected system from smartphone to focused
wearable display.
Resolved device
The final direction packages the electronics as a
compact, glanceable object that reduces visual clutter
and keeps the rider present on the road.
